stances.summary: Questions tight labor market claims despite job growth
stances.quote:
Employers seems able to hire all the workers that they want, so is this a tight labor market? 
Long-term unemployment is still rising, job growth has been concentrated in just a few industries. 
And yet, wow, +172K is impressive. And the 3-month average is even more impressive.

stances.summary: Criticizes policy creating permanent economic underclass
stances.quote: It’s almost like they want to create a permanent underclass.

stances.summary: Supports tariff elimination as tax cut alternative to unilateral action
stances.quote: I hear the President plans to announce a tax cut for American businesses and people that he's doing without Congress. Some argue he can't cut taxes without Congress, but he can: Ending all of his tariffs would be a big tax cut for American companies and workers. Fingers crossed!

stances.summary: Skeptical of tariff refunds, expects continued legal battle over presidential authority
stances.quote: The only certainty we got today is only that IEEPA does not give the president sweeping powers to levy tariffs. We are not done in the tariff battle. And refunds? I'm not going to hold my breath.

stances.summary: Opposes unchecked presidential tariff authority, demands Congressional action
stances.quote: Tariffs are taxes and that means without the tariffs there is a revenue problem, but that doesn't mean we should give the President broad authority to tax whoever he wants whoever much he wants. Congress needs to act.

stances.summary: Highlights significant energy price surge affecting inflation index
stances.quote: Most people don’t need the BLS to tell them that energy prices are up, but still…the largest one month gain in the energy index in 21 years. Pushing the entire index up 0.9 percent in one month.

stances.summary: Supports healthy debate about Federal Reserve policy
stances.quote: This is the kind of debate around Fed policy that is normal and healthy.

stances.summary: Warns Trump's European tariffs pose serious risks despite modest market decline
stances.quote: The markets are only down 1-2% but don't let that lull you into thinking that what Trump is doing in Europe isn't that bad. They've priced in a high probablility that he'll back down.

stances.summary: Implies wealth concentration matters for policy outcomes
stances.quote:
It does matter who holds the wealth.

stances.summary: Warns wars reduce living standards broadly
stances.quote: Wars are times of declining living standards for everyone.

stances.summary: Warns Iran war will raise energy and transportation costs
stances.quote: Core inflation excludes food and energy, it’s too soon for those prices to be impacted by the Iran war, but that doesn’t mean they won’t be. Higher energy prices ultimately effects the cost of making and transporting many things.

stances.summary: Criticizes Trump as departing from traditional GOP free-trade, anti-tax positions
stances.quote: Traditionally the GOP was the anti-tax, free-trade party, the is the first GOP President to be anti-competition, pro-tax, at least on consumers and small businesses.

stances.summary: Notes gendered insult pattern, sees progress in equal application
stances.quote: Honestly, I thought this was the kind of insult reserved for women—diminutive first naming or misspelled first naming—so the silver lining is that it is nice to see that it is not a completely gendered form of insult!

stances.summary: Supports federal guarantee of paid time off for workers
stances.quote:
An overwhelming majority of American workers—over 90 percent—support the right to earned time off.  

@betseystevenson.bsky.social explains what a federal guarantee of earned paid time off could look like—and how it would benefit all workers: www.hamiltonproject.org/publication/.
